correctness.rationale: Corner removal gives R=1−sum_i c_i(1−t_(i−1))t_i. In diagonal coordinates the absolute normalized corner areas are p,q,1−p,1−q, so sum c_i=2 and sum c_i c_(i+1)=1. With x_i=t_i−1/2, the centered area is the sum of linear terms (c_(i+1)−c_i)x_i/2 and bilinear terms c_i x_(i−1)x_i. These terms are pairwise orthogonal by independence and centering; their variance is sum (c_(i+1)−c_i)^2/48+sum c_i^2/144, giving exactly the claimed expression. Every (p,q) in the open unit square occurs, so the extrema and equality statement follow. At equality the two sums of opposite uniform parameters minus one give the independent triangular factors. Integrating the product density gives the quoted CDF, including H(0)=0 and H(1)=−1/2; expanding the bracket at z=1 gives (1−z)^3/6 and hence the integrated lower-tail coefficient 4/3. The centered moments follow from integrating the triangular density. The coordinate chart in the frozen proof has clockwise rather than counterclockwise turns in the usual orientation; all turns have the same nonzero sign and the computation uses absolute areas, so the slip does not change convexity, admissibility, or the formula.
residual_risks: The supplied Monte Carlo stage uses the corner formula as a generator; it is not independent evidence for that identity. The exact shoelace comparisons are finite; the proof supplies universality.

evidence: The indexed November 1 recurrence covers every iteration of precisely the same four-side update. Nguyen–Volkov already use the same update, with general iid side fractions, but the results inspected concern eventual shape flatness and Lyapunov rates. Reitzner et al. sample points uniformly on the entire boundary and analyze large-sample hull asymptotics.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The newer moment recurrence strictly contains the frozen variance identity. The earlier general subdivision construction and asymptotics do not provide the one-step variance coefficient or parallelogram product law; whole-boundary sampling changes the experiment.

value.rationale: For a natural stratified experiment the variance is an exact scalar measure of failure of diagonal bisection, including a sharp degenerating supremum. At the unique minimum family the complete density identifies a logarithmic center and a quartic rare-event law. These are useful benchmarks for one-step polygon subdivision beyond the elementary mean or a square-only calculation.
residual_risks: No complete law for arbitrary non-parallelograms or an iid whole-boundary experiment is established.
